summary.text: A 20-year-old Chinese man of Han ethnicity had cutaneous and soft-tissue venous malformations first noted at 18 months of age and recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding since early childhood. At 7 years of age, a systematic gastrointestinal evaluation showed multiple intestinal venous malformations and led to partial intestinal resection; postoperative pathology contributed to the diagnosis of blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome, and other vascular syndromes and tumors were considered unlikely or excluded.

Between 7 and 15 years of age bleeding with melena, hematochezia and progressive anemia continued; he needed multiple transfusions, endoscopic ligation, further intestinal resections and excision of soft-tissue masses, which gave temporary relief before bleeding recurred. At 17 years of age he was admitted with worsening hematochezia, palpitations and fatigue and hemoglobin 34 g/L; endoscopy and MRI showed venous malformations, and he had endoscopic sclerotherapy, open adhesiolysis and intestinal excision with uneventful recovery.

At 20 years of age he was admitted with recurrent melena and fatigue for 2 months; he was markedly anemic with superficial bluish masses and healed scars, hemoglobin 55 g/L, and no family history, allergies, smoking or alcohol use. During the admission he received packed red-cell transfusion, oral hematinic and hemostatic therapy and multiple sessions of percutaneous lauromacrogol sclerotherapy, without gastrointestinal endoscopic therapy or intestinal resection.

At discharge he was clinically stable with hemoglobin 98 g/L and no documented treatment-related complications. Follow-up at 2 weeks, 1 month and 2 months after discharge reported no recurrent melena or hematochezia, no further transfusion requirement, continued oral iron supplementation and hemoglobin 113 g/L at 2 months; no systemic therapy was given and genetic testing was not performed.
